verdict.rationale: Cloudflare's own docs claim Workers fits existing workflows (Git, GitHub Actions, VS Code, any framework) and list support for mainstream frameworks and languages. However, the creation, development and deployment path documented here runs through Cloudflare's own Wrangler CLI and create-cloudflare scaffolder. A community report also notes Cloudflare-specific services like KV and D1 create lock-in, which tempers the "no proprietary tools" claim. Missing for 10: documented Git/CI integration details (e.g., GitHub Actions setup guides), evidence that deployment works without Cloudflare-specific tooling like Wrangler, and independent hands-on corroboration of the workflow-portability claim.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Fits into your existing workflows: Git, GitHub Actions, VS Code, and any framework. No proprietary tools or vendor lock-in.
